title: Validating LLM-Based Essay Scorers: A Comparative Analysis in Critical Online Reasoning in Medical Education
abstract: arXiv:2611.21208v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated essay scorers (AES) based on large language models (LLMs) promise human-level accuracy. However, training, fine-tuning, and evaluating LLMs for specific assessment tasks is costly. In particular, the question arises whether these AES should be trained for specific domains or whether models based on generic LLMs might be sufficient. Human annotations, by contrast, are often more valid but far more expensive. This study evaluates whether ensembles of AES systems based on general-purpose LLMs can approximate human ratings of medical-education writing tasks by leveraging encoded linguistic and conceptual knowledge. The goal is to assess whether general-purpose models are applicable for assisting or potentially replacing human annotation in this domain. translated_title: 基于大语言模型的作文评分器验证：医学教育中批判性在线推理的比较分析
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的自动作文评分器（AES）有望达到人类水平的准确性。然而，针对特定评估任务对LLM进行训练、微调和评估的成本很高。尤其是，这些AES是否应该针对特定领域进行训练，还是基于通用LLM的模型就已经足够，是一个值得探讨的问题。相比之下，人工标注通常更为有效，但成本也高得多。本研究评估了基于通用LLM的AES系统集合，能否利用其编码的语言和概念知识来近似人类对医学教育写作任务的评分。其目标是评估通用模型是否适用于辅助、甚至潜在地取代该领域的人工标注。我们试验了11个AES系统和8个不同的LLM，评估了668份学生对12个任务的回答，并采用了7名人类标注者进行的2076次评估。这些评分被汇总……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本研究验证了基于通用大语言模型的自动作文评分系统集合能够近似人类对医学教育写作任务的评分，表明通用模型有望辅助甚至替代昂贵的人工标注。
en_tdlr: This study validates that ensembles of automated essay scoring systems based on general-purpose LLMs can approximate human ratings of medical education writing tasks, suggesting general-purpose models could assist or potentially replace costly human annotation.
